title: CaseFlow Legal Intake POC 1 SOW & Pricing Sketch
content:
Overview:

This note frames a proposed 6-week proof-of-concept for Barton & Meyers LLP to evaluate Redwood Inference for confidential case intake: automated summarization, privilege-aware redaction, and structured extraction to populate matter records. The emphasis is on a private deployment pattern (customer VPC / on-prem) with KMS-managed keys and minimal data egress. This is a working sketch for the SOW and includes workshop takeaways and a high-level pricing/packaging sketch.

Objectives:
- Demonstrate high-utility summaries and chronological extraction over a canonical test set (~2,000 documents including scanned PDFs).
- Provide redaction tooling that attorneys can approve with an audit trail and rollback (human-in-the-loop).
- Validate performance on a dedicated inference node: target median latency <700 ms for 512-token summaries and ability to complete nightly batch of 2k docs in <2 hours.
- Produce an operational runbook that maps to Redwood Private deployment patterns and customer security controls.

Acceptance criteria (POC):
- Qualitative sign-off from 3 subject-matter attorneys on a 100-doc sample (accept/reject for summaries).
- Redaction: >=98% precision for PII markers on a 250-doc validation set; false redactions of privilege phrases <2%.
- Perf: nightly batch completes in target window; interactive median latency target met.
- Security: KMS integration validated; no customer data retained outside customer control plane during POC.

Scope & Timeline (6 weeks):
Week 0  Kickoff and data prep
- Align on goals, approved test data, contacts, and legal constraints.
- Customer to provide sanitized sample set (min 2k docs) and metadata mapping for matter types.

Week 1  Private infra setup
- Deploy private control plane or hybrid agent in customer VPC / on-prem host.
- Configure KMS/HSM, ingress/egress rules, telemetry hooks (Prometheus/ELK), smoke tests.

Weeks 22  Model workflows and extraction
- Implement summarization prompts and extraction schemas; tune redaction classifier rules and heuristics.
- Integrate OCR pipeline (customer-supplied or recommended third-party) and validate preprocessing.

Week 4  HIL review UI and audit trail
- Deliver a lightweight web UI for attorney verification and redaction approval with audit export.
- Connect SSO test tenant and RBAC sample.

Week 5  Load validation and runbook
- Run batch and interactive load tests; produce latency/throughput report and incident playbook.

Week 6  Handoff and acceptance
- Demo, knowledge transfer, and handoff of configs, prompts, and runbook.

Deliverables:
- Deployment artifacts (Terraform snippets / helm values) and runbook
- Prompt library, extraction schema, and redaction policy examples
- Attorney verification UI prototype and integration notes
- Performance report and production cost estimate options
- POC wrap-up deck and acceptance checklist

Estimated professional services (POC):
- SE engagement: 4 FTE-weeks (approx. 160 hours) across discovery, infra, and product engineering.
- Fixed-fee POC estimate: $48,000 (covers SE time, dev/test infra, one security review, and workshop facilitation).

Indicative production options & pricing:
1) Redwood Private (customer VPC) + Dedicated Capacity
- Production onboarding PS: 23 weeks, $35k60k depending on integration depth.
- Dedicated capacity: from $15k/month for a small dedicated GPU pool (profile varies by throughput & latency SLOs).
- Optional premium support / SLOs: $6k12k/month.

2) On-prem appliance (air-gapped)
- One-time license & packaging: from $120k (includes offline control plane & hardening).
- On-prem PS: $50k90k for install, validation, and HSM integration.

3) Hybrid (hosted control plane + customer inference nodes)
- Lower upfront: $20k setup, $10k/month for inference usage + reserved burst credits.

Pricing notes:
- Estimates assume same model family & quantization as POC; changes in SLOs or scale will alter hardware and cost profiles.
- On-prem packages include 12-month maintenance; extended terms priced separately.

Workshop notes (2025-09-10 session):
Attendees: Barton & Meyers  Sarah Barton (COO), Kevin Doyle (IT), Heather Yao (Lead Attorney); Redwood  Ava Martinez (SE), Jonah Chen (infra), Priya Kapoor (product).
Decisions:
- Customer preference: on-prem / air-gapped for regulatory reasons; hybrid acceptable if KMS & egress controls meet policy.
- Fine-tuning: excluded from base POC. We will focus on prompt engineering and lightweight classifier tuning; any model training requiring off-prem data will require separate legal/contract sign-off.
Open actions:
- Kevin to share network diagram & available GPU/node specs (due 2025-09-15).
- Redwood to provide threat model doc and controls table, plus SAML/KMS integration checklist.
- Legal to provide canonical list of phrases protected from redaction (due 2025-09-12).

Risks & mitigations:
- Data leakage: Mitigate using private control plane, KMS, and strict egress filtering; add legal review.
- Hallucination of legal facts: Use conservative prompting patterns, require attorney verification for critical outputs, and include citation extraction where possible.
- OCR quality: Poor OCR reduces extraction accuracy; recommend customer validates OCR pipeline or supply high-quality text extracts.

Assumptions:
- Customer provides representative, sanitized test corpus and timely infra access.
- Redwood will not retain customer data outside the customer's private control plane during POC unless explicitly authorized.
- Security contacts available for KMS/HSM integration and network approvals.

Immediate next steps:
1) Redwood to deliver 1-page production options comparison (due 2025-09-19).
2) Customer to provide node inventory & sample data (due 2025-09-15).
3) Align and sign POC SOW (target sign-off 2025-09-22).

End of note.
